strategyReview: One-touch NO selling-YES edge continues to perform well both live and in shadows, with the recent cluster of losses due to compressed edge rather than structural failure. Weekend funding reversion long remains the strongest signal family with 74% win rate and high aggregate PnL, though some single-name shadows (HOOD, AAPL) underperform. Funding extreme long struggles on AMZN and HYPE, dragging overall performance, while extreme short is moderately positive on AMZN but net flat. P/C ratio signals show asset heterogeneity: extreme low is profitable on BTC/OIL but terrible on AMZN; extreme high is mediocre. The portfolio is marginally profitable but concentrated edge opportunities exist in one-touch and weekend funding families that should be promoted to live signals.

journalEntry: Tonight's analysis confirms the strong performance of the weekend funding reversion long shadow, which should be promoted to a live signal lane immediately given 253 resolved shadows with 74% win rate and +2.5% total PnL. The one-touch NO edge family also shows consistent profitability across assets, with OIL near-expiry 1-3pt edge cluster (90% WR) and broad 3-8pt edge cluster (67% WR) ready for shadow-to-live promotion with appropriate risk management. Informed flow asymmetry (FIND-0020) suggests fading dumb money on high-strike NO contracts could be a powerful overlay. Conversely, funding extreme long on AMZN/HYPE and P/C extreme high on BTC are underperforming and should remain disabled or have asset-specific stop adjustments. Several weekend funding shadows on individual names are failing but the aggregate signal remains robust; do not gate the main signal by single-asset performance. The GOLD one-touch heatmap hypothesis (H-534) is a confirmed failure and should be killed. No parameter changes recommended at this time; the risk settings for active signals are appropriate.
